algorithm: Fixed-size word chunking with overlap, TF-IDF-weighted term-overlap retrieval, extractive answer from the top chunk with citation.
complexity: O(C*T) to score C chunks against T query terms; IDF build is O(total tokens).
data_flow_ascii:
documents -> chunk_documents (size/overlap) -> chunks
chunks -> IDF table -> score_chunk per query -> retrieve top-k
top chunk -> generate_answer -> answer text + citation
description_sentence: A retrieval-augmented generation pipeline simulator that chunks documents, retrieves passages with TF-IDF-style scoring, and answers extractively with citations.
failure_note: A query with no overlapping terms scores zero everywhere and returns a graceful 'no relevant passage' answer instead of guessing.

functions.desc: Split documents into fixed-size word chunks with overlap; returns chunk dicts.
functions.name: chunk_documents
functions.signature: chunk_documents(documents: list, chunk_size: int = 40, overlap: int = 10) -> list

functions.desc: TF-IDF-style term-overlap score of one chunk for the query terms.
functions.name: score_chunk
functions.signature: score_chunk(chunk_tokens: list, query_terms: list, idf: dict) -> float

functions.desc: Rank chunks by score_chunk and return the top-k with scores.
functions.name: retrieve
functions.signature: retrieve(chunks: list, query: str, idf: dict, k: int = 3) -> list

functions.desc: Return the top-ranked chunk as the answer plus a citation string.
functions.name: generate_answer
functions.signature: generate_answer(query: str, chunks: list, idf: dict, k: int = 2) -> dict

functions.desc: Seeded end-to-end demo: corpus, chunks, ranked hits, answer, citation.
functions.name: run_demo
functions.signature: run_demo(seed: int, query: str = None) -> int

functions.desc: Build the command-line parser for the demo.
functions.name: build_parser

functions.desc: Entry point: seeded RAG pipeline demo.
functions.name: main

label: rag_simulator
output_shape: Prints chunk counts, the top-3 ranked passages with scores, and the extractive answer with its citation.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that chunks documents, retrieves the most relevant passages with TF-IDF scoring, and answers with citations.

qa.a: Term frequency inside the chunk times inverse document frequency across chunks; rare query terms count more than common ones.
Overlap keeps sentences that straddle a boundary inside at least one chunk, so retrieval does not lose context at cut points.
Yes: score_chunk is pure, and retrieve just sorts, so any chunk list and IDF table work, including ones from real documents.
qa.q: Can this run on real documents?

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python implementing chunking, TF-IDF retrieval, and citation-backed extractive answering over a seeded corpus.
run_notes: --query overrides the seeded demo query; chunk size and overlap come from the project params.
scaling_note: In-memory chunk list suits thousands of chunks; millions would need an inverted index instead of per-query rescoring.
storage_note: No persistence: the corpus, chunks, and IDF table are rebuilt from the seed on every run.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, random, math, re, collections
tradeoff_note: Term overlap is transparent and fast but misses paraphrases that embedding retrieval would catch.
